svg.text: Windows 3.1 kernel architecture: Standard mode vs 386 Enhanced mode
WIN /S · DOSX.EXE + KRNL286.EXE · no virtual memory, no V86
Windows environment (protected mode, one address space)
window manager, graphics, segment move / discard, task scheduler
display, mouse, keyboard, COMM, TIMER, wave / MIDI
Memory: segments moved / discarded, no swap file (up to 16 MB RAM)
Scheduling: cooperative. A Win16 app must yield.
full screen, runs ALONE; Windows is swapped out meanwhile
provides DPMI-style services, switches CPU between modes
called by switching back to real mode
Hardware: CPU, RAM, disk, display, sound card
WIN /3 · WIN386.EXE (VMM + VxDs) + KRNL386.EXE · paging, V86
All Win16 apps share this ONE VM.
inside it. VMM may page it.
Hardware: CPU (386+), RAM, disk, display, sound card
IRQ -> VPICD -> reflected into the owning VM. Port I/O from a VM is trapped by the owning VxD.
The same Win16 app runs in both modes. Standard mode: DOS runs ALONE in real mode. Enhanced mode: Windows is just one VM; DOS boxes run beside it.
Drawn from knowledge of Win3.x internals, simplified. Check details against the Windows 3.1 DDK.
